note: The attacker-controlled JSON is decoded into an ExpandedNodeId with a bytestring NodeId and a namespace URI string.
Decoding allocates heap-backed storage for both the nested bytestring identifier and the namespace URI.
The decoder populates a nested NodeId plus namespaceUri from attacker-controlled JSON fields.
Cleanup of ExpandedNodeId frees the nested NodeId and namespace URI through their respective clear helpers.
The nested NodeId releases its heap-backed bytestring identifier first.
The identifier buffer is freed here, creating the first free in the candidate chain.
The generic clear dispatcher walks the decoded object graph and invokes the nested frees on the attacker-controlled structure.
A second access to the same heap-backed identifier storage during recursive cleanup is the memory-safety sink.
The namespace URI string is also freed during the same unwind, so any aliasing bug would surface here as well.
The sink is the second free/read of already-released heap storage during cleanup of the decoded ExpandedNodeId object.
